{{Short description|Result of multiplying five instances of a number together}}
In [[arithmetic]] and [[algebra]], the '''fifth power''' or '''sursolid'''<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.websters1913.com/words/Sursolid | title=Webster's 1913 }}</ref> of a [[number]] ''n'' is the result of multiplying five instances of ''n'' together:
:{{math|size=120%|1=''n''<sup>5</sup> = ''n'' × ''n'' × ''n'' × ''n'' × ''n''}}.

Fifth [[exponentiation|powers]] are also formed by multiplying a number by its [[fourth power]], or the [[square number|square]] of a number by its [[cube (algebra)|cube]].

The sequence of fifth powers of [[integer]]s is:
:0, 1, 32, 243, 1024, 3125, 7776, 16807, 32768, 59049, 100000, 161051, 248832, 371293, 537824, 759375, 1048576, 1419857, 1889568, 2476099, 3200000, 4084101, 5153632, 6436343, 7962624, 9765625, ... {{OEIS|id=A000584}}

==Properties==

For any integer ''n'', the last [[decimal]] digit of ''n''<sup>5</sup> is the same as the last (decimal) digit of ''n'', i.e. 
:<math> n \equiv n^5\pmod {10}</math>

By the [[Abel–Ruffini theorem]], there is no general [[algebraic formula]] (formula expressed in terms of [[radical expression]]s) for the solution of [[polynomial equation]]s containing a fifth power of the [[unknown (mathematics)|unknown]] as their highest power. This is the lowest power for which this is true. See [[quintic equation]], [[sextic equation]], and [[septic equation]].

Along with the fourth power, the fifth power is one of two powers ''k'' that can be expressed as the sum of ''k''&nbsp;−&thinsp;1 other ''k''-th powers, providing counterexamples to [[Euler's sum of powers conjecture]]. Specifically, 

:{{math|27<sup>5</sup> + 84<sup>5</sup> + 110<sup>5</sup> + 133<sup>5</sup> {{=}} 144<sup>5</sup>}}  (Lander & Parkin, 1966)<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lander |first1=L. J. |last2=Parkin |first2=T. R. |year=1966 |title=Counterexample to Euler's conjecture on sums of like powers |journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. |doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1966-11654-3 |volume=72 |issue=6 |page=1079|doi-access=free }}</ref>
